item.title: ASML mit Rekordumsatz und vollen Auftragsbüchern
item.description: Eine unverändert robuste Nachfrage verhilft ASML zu einem erneuten Umsatz- und Gewinnsprung. Daraufhin legte der weltgrößte Anbieter von Halbleiter-Produktionsanlagen am Mittwoch einen überraschend optimistischen Ausblick für das laufende Quartal vor. "Wir haben einen Rekordumsatz am oberen Ende unserer Zielspanne erwirtschaftet", sagte Konzernchef Christophe Fouquet. Ein Ende des aktuellen Wachstums sei nicht in Sicht. Die Auftragsbücher für 2028 seien bereits gut gefüllt. Einige Kunden wollten bereits Bestellungen für 2029 und 2030 aufgeben.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eine unverändert robuste Nachfrage verhilft ASML (ASML.AS) zu einem erneuten Umsatz- und Gewinnsprung. Daraufhin legte der weltgrößte Anbieter von Halbleiter-Produktionsanlagen am Mittwoch einen überraschend optimistischen Ausblick für das laufende Quartal vor. "Wir haben einen Rekordumsatz am oberen Ende unserer Zielspanne erwirtschaftet", sagte Konzernchef Christophe Fouquet. Ein Ende des aktuellen Wachstums sei nicht in Sicht. Die Auftragsbücher für 2028 seien bereits gut gefüllt. Einige Kunden wollten bereits Bestellungen für 2029 und 2030 aufgeben. Das wertvollste börsennotierte Unternehmen Europas steigerte den Umsatz im dritten Quartal um mehr als die Hälfte auf 11,66 Milliarden Euro. Der Reingewinn verdoppelte sich nahezu auf 4,96 Milliarden Euro und lag deutlich über den Markterwartungen. Vor allem das Geschäft mit der Modernisierung bereits installierter Anlagen habe sich überraschend stark entwickelt, erläuterte Fouquet. Auf Grundlage dieser Zahlen kündigte der niederländische Konzern eine Zwischendividende von 1,88 Euro je Aktie an. Für das laufende Quartal stellte ASML Erlöse zwischen 14,2 und 15,2 Milliarden Euro sowie eine Bruttomarge von 57 Prozent in Aussicht. Analysten hatten mit 14,19 Milliarden Euro beziehungsweise 55,4 Prozent gerechnet. Das Unternehmen präzisierte darüber hinaus sein Wachstumsziel für 2026. Es erwartet nun einen Umsatz zwischen 44 und 45 Milliarden Euro. Bislang hatte es eine Spanne von [USN:L8N43H0I7 TEXT:"43 bis 45 Milliarden Euro"] prognostiziert. ASML-Finanzchef Roger Dassen kündigte zudem für 2027 Preiserhöhungen an, die sich ab 2028 vollständig in der Bilanz niederschlagen würden. "Es gab Befürchtungen, dass der KI-Boom an Schwung verlieren könnte", sagte Gordon Kerr, Anlagestratege der Ratingagentur KBRA. Die Zahlen von ASML untermauerten jedoch die Einschätzung, dass die Chip-Nachfrage ungebrochen sei und der Bauboom bei Rechenzentren bis weit ins Jahr 2027 anhalten werde. ASML-Aktien stiegen an der Amsterdamer Börse um bis zu 3,6 Prozent. In ihrem Windschatten legte der europäische Technologie-Index (.SX8P) zeitweise 1,6 Prozent zu. UNANGEFOCHTENER WELTMARKTFÜHRER ASML beherrscht Schätzungen zufolge 94 Prozent des Weltmarktes für Lithographie-Anlagen. Der Konzern setzt dabei als einziger auf [USN:L8N4511QW TEXT:"extrem ultraviolettes Licht"] (EUV). Mithilfe dieser Technologie können die Maschinen - jede so groß wie ein Doppeldeckerbus und etwa 400 Millionen Dollar teuer - besonders feine Schaltkreise auf Silizium-Wafer brennen. Dadurch werden Halbleiter kleiner und leistungsfähiger. Zu den wichtigsten Kunden von ASML zählen der Auftragsfertiger TSMC (2330.TW) sowie die Chipkonzerne Intel (INTC.O) und Samsung (005930.KS) . Angesichts der rasant wachsenden Nachfrage nach modernen Hochleistungsprozessoren dürften EUV-Anlagen für 2027 bereits komplett ausverkauft sein, schrieb Analyst Sandeep Deshpande von der Bank JPMorgan. Daher will ASML seine Produktionskapazitäten in den kommenden beiden Jahren um jeweils 30 Prozent erweitern. Dies gelte sowohl für die modernen EUV-Maschinen als auch für die Vorgänger-Generation, die mit tief ultraviolettem Licht (DUV) arbeitet. Fouquet betonte jedoch, dass die bisherigen Ausbauziele nicht ausreichend seien. Der Konzern dürfe dabei jedoch die Nachfrageentwicklung nicht aus den Augen verlieren, warnte Nick Rossolillo, Gründer des Finanzdienstleisters und ASML-Aktionärs Chip Stock Investor. Ein gebremster Ausbau biete ein Polster für das unvermeidliche Abflauen der Branchenkonjunktur. Im vergangenen Monat hatte ASML den Grundstein für ein neues Werk in Eindhoven gelegt, dessen erste Ausbaustufe 2029 fertiggestellt werden soll. CHINA-GESCHÄFT BLEIBT SORGENKIND Ein Wermutstropfen waren die unverändert unklaren Aussichten für das China-Geschäft. ASML macht bislang etwa 20 Prozent seines Umsatzes in der Volksrepublik, obwohl das Unternehmen auf Druck der USA seine EUV-Geräte nicht dorthin liefern darf. Die Regierung in Washington will damit den technologischen und militärischen Aufstieg Chinas bremsen. Einem US-Gesetzentwurf zufolge soll künftig auch der Verkauf von DUV-Anlagen sowie die Wartung bereits verkaufter Maschinen verboten werden. ASML-Manager Dassen kritisierte diese Pläne als kontraproduktiv. China werde in diesem Fall die heimische Entwicklung von Lithographie-Systemen forcieren. Er sei jedoch optimistisch, dass in den USA "der gesunde Menschenverstand siegen" werde.

item.title: MPS investors should reject twin bids, special dividend, proxy advisers say
item.description: Leading governance advisers Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis urged shareholders in Monte dei Paschi di Siena to reject proposed bids to buy Banco BPM and Banca Generali at an upcoming vote.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Leading governance advisers Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis urged shareholders in Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS.MI) to reject proposed bids to buy Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and Banca Generali (BGN.MI) at an upcoming vote. MPS investors meet on October 29 to vote on the plan, which is CEO Luigi Lovaglio's defence scheme against a takeover offer by Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) . Intesa has bid for MPS and would then sell half of its branches to resolve antitrust issues, a break-up prospect MPS opposes. In a report released late on Tuesday, ISS said MPS investors were "being asked to vote on a vision that contemplates doubling the bank's size through two deals in the midst of integrating the prior transformational acquisition of Mediobanca". Glass Lewis said in a report on Wednesday that its recommendation to reject Lovaglio's defence plan stemmed mainly from the need "to critically preserve investor optionality at an exceptionally impactful juncture". Intesa a week ago sweetened its bid on condition MPS shareholders vote against the counter plan on October 29, warning it otherwise intends to make use of clauses allowing it to drop its takeover offer. Glass Lewis noted that a group of key MPS investors had already sided with Intesa following the ultimatum, and that Banco BPM's main shareholder Credit Agricole (CAGR.PA) had also rejected the MPS bid. Both ISS and Glass Lewis recommended that shareholders back the merger of Mediobanca with MPS, while voting against a special dividend distribution connected to the twin bids. ISS said the Intesa offer "was not without concerns of its own". However, "even when viewed in isolation, the facts and disclosure do not support the proposed deals". Glass Lewis also urged investors not to back the appointment of Alessandro Caltagirone, son of leading MPS shareholder Francesco Gaetano Caltagirone, to the bank's board.

item.title: Turkish prosecutors appoint government trustee to run pro-opposition Halk TV
item.description: Turkish authorities appointed a government trustee to run pro-opposition broadcaster Halk TV, prosecutors said on Wednesday, as police raided its Istanbul office, extending a crackdown on the opposition and prompting fresh concerns over media freedom.
item.dc:creator: Tuvan Gumrukcu
item.content:encoded: Turkish authorities appointed a government trustee to run pro-opposition broadcaster Halk TV, prosecutors said on Wednesday, as police raided its Istanbul office, extending a crackdown on the opposition and prompting fresh concerns over media freedom. The Istanbul Chief Prosecutor's Office said its financial crimes unit had conducted an investigation into Halk TV Chairman Cafer Mahiroglu over "bribery, tender-rigging, and laundering of assets derived from crime", adding that evidence, witness statements and transaction records showed criminal activity. Prosecutors ordered the detention of 17 people, including Mahiroglu, and 11 have been detained, the statement said, adding that firms linked to Mahiroglu were seized and the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (TMSF) appointed as trustee. Mahiroglu, who is currently outside Turkey, is being sought by the authorities. The channel's live broadcast was cut at 6:30 a.m. (0330 GMT), after which pre-recorded material began airing. It said on its website that "hundreds of police" were inside and entry into the premises was not being permitted. A Halk TV programmer said negotiations with the trustee delegation to continue broadcasts had yielded no results. The move comes days after Kemal Kilicdaroglu, the court-appointed chairman of Turkey's former main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP), publicly criticised Halk TV and Mahiroglu over its coverage. He said the CHP had complained to Turkey's RTUK television watchdog but no action was taken. Kilicdaroglu lost the CHP leadership to Ozgur Ozel in 2023, but was [USN:L6N41Y0ZX TEXT:"reinstated by a court ruling"] in May amid an [USN:L6N42B0TW TEXT:"unprecedented legal crackdown"] on the opposition. He has refused to call new party elections, while his rhetoric has become more aligned with the government. The CHP later criticised Wednesday's raid on Halk TV as a "shameful" example of "systematic pressure" on opposition media and said its own complaints about the broadcaster's coverage were a "natural part of democratic life". CRACKDOWN ON PRESS FREEDOM Wednesday's move makes Halk TV the fifth major Turkish news outlet to have a trustee appointed, following similar legal decisions for Flash TV, Eko Turk, Haberturk and Tele1. Authorities have appointed trustees in recent years to take over municipalities and companies. It has long appointed trustees to seize municipalities run by elected pro-Kurdish opposition mayors in southeastern Turkey and has more recently taken similar steps in major municipalities - including Istanbul and its districts - won by the opposition, prompting some mayors [USN:L8N45T0JQ TEXT:"to join"] President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party. Rights groups and Western countries [USN:L6N45V0M3 TEXT:"have criticised"] the government over its use of the judiciary, its record on rights, and crackdown on press freedom in recent years as it establishes tighter control over mainstream media. Several opposition or independent outlets have experienced access bans, fines, and other [USN:L6N45M0VP TEXT:"restrictions"]. The government says Turkey's judiciary is independent. It has not commented publicly on the latest moves against Halk TV. Ozel, who now leads the main opposition [USN:L6N43Q11G TEXT:"New Party"], condemned Wednesday's move, as did the pro-Kurdish opposition DEM Party. "Dawn raid on a television channel, appointing a trustee — only dictators would do such a thing," Ozel said on X. "Those who appoint trustees to municipalities and trample the people's will have now appointed a trustee to Halk TV, watched by millions. Because THEY ARE IMPOTENT AND COWARDS!" The raid on Halk TV came as Erdogan's biggest political rival, [USN:L6N44A0AK TEXT:"jailed Istanbul Mayor"] Ekrem Imamoglu, was expected to start his defence on Wednesday in a [USN:L6N3ZX0H5 TEXT:"sweeping corruption trial"] of more than 400 defendants linked to the Istanbul municipality.

item.title: FMI-Washington doit réduire son déficit et la Chine augmenter sa consommation intérieure
item.description: Les États-Unis ne peuvent sortir de la spirale de l'endettement avec la seule croissance économique, Washington n'ayant pas d'autre choix que de procéder à des ajustements fiscaux ou budgétaires, a déclaré mercredi la directrice générale du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Les États-Unis ne peuvent sortir de la spirale de l'endettement avec la seule croissance économique, Washington n'ayant pas d'autre choix que de procéder à des ajustements fiscaux ou budgétaires, a déclaré mercredi la directrice générale du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva. S'exprimant à l'occasion des réunions annuelles du FMI et de la Banque mondiale qui se tiennent cette semaine à Bangkok, elle a également soutenu que la Chine devait cesser de dépendre des exportations pour s'orienter davantage vers la consommation intérieure. La directrice de l'organisation financière exhorte ainsi les deux plus grandes économies mondiales à changer radicalement de cap afin de réduire les déséquilibres budgétaires et commerciaux. Ces déclarations font écho à celles du directeur du département des finances publiques du FMI, Rodrigo Valdes, qui a souligné plus tôt ce mercredi que l'inflation, les niveaux élevés d'endettement et la flambée des rendements obligataires avaient accentué l'urgence d'un assainissement budgétaire à l'échelle mondiale. Kristalina Georgieva a désigné les économies avancées, à savoir les États-Unis et les pays européens, comme les "pires contrevenants" en matière d'endettement, la hausse des taux d'intérêt de référence ayant des répercussions sur les pays à faibles revenus, déjà contraints par les marchés financiers à maîtriser leur dette. Interrogée lors d'une conférence de presse sur la nécessité pour Washington d'adopter une politique budgétaire plus restrictive, la patronne du FMI a répondu que le secrétaire au Trésor américain, Scott Bessent, reconnaissait que les niveaux de déficit et d'endettement des États-Unis étaient trop élevés et devaient être maîtrisés. "Les autorités comptent beaucoup sur une forte croissance aux États-Unis (...) Au FMI, nous estimons que la croissance aide bien sûr, mais qu'elle ne permet pas d'opérer les ajustements nécessaires assez rapidement. Certaines mesures (budgétaires, NDLR) seraient donc nécessaires", a-t-elle ajouté. Début août, le département du Trésor américain a la dette totale des États-Unis a dépassé pour la première fois les [USN:L6N44G191 TEXT:"40.000 milliards de dollar"]s - ce qui représenté quelque 123% du PIB 2026 estimé de la première économie mondiale. MESSAGE URGENT L'appel à une action plus résolue pour réduire la dette est également au coeur du rapport "Fiscal Monitor", publié ce mercredi par le FMI, qui souligne que tout retard dans ces efforts ne fait que compliquer la tâche pour les années à venir. "Nous avons renforcé le caractère urgent de notre message", a dit mercredi Rodrigo Valdes, qui estime que la flambée des rendements obligataires laisse aux gouvernements une marge de manoeuvre budgétaire très réduite. "Les résultats budgétaires de cette année sont pires que prévu il y a six mois et pires qu'il y a un an", avait-t-il déclaré lors d'un entretien accordé à Reuters l'occasion de la réunion du FMI dans la capitale thaïlandaise. La flambée des prix du pétrole dans le contexte de la guerre au Moyen-Orient, une demande d'investissement plus soutenue et une croissance du secteur de l'IA plus forte que prévu ont entraîné une forte hausse des rendements souverains à long terme ces derniers mois. La France a été particulièrement touchée par ces tensions ces dernières semaines, alors qu'elle peine à maîtriser son déficit budgétaire, supérieur à 5% du produit intérieur brut (PIB). Le rendement moyen des obligations d'État des pays du G7 à 10 ans a quant à lui progressé de plus de 110 points de base entre février et septembre, atteignant son plus haut niveau en près de vingt ans, selon le FMI. L'organisation estime en outre que le coût moyen effectif du financement public devrait atteindre 3,7% d'ici 2031, contre 2,3% en 2021. ABSENCE DE BESSENT Le secrétaire au Trésor américain ne participe pas aux réunions annuelles de Bangkok, la campagne pour les élections de mi-mandat s'intensifiant, et ce bien que les États-Unis assurent cette année la présidence du G20. Scott Bessent a joué le rôle de porte-parole principal des politiques économiques du président Donald Trump, vantant notamment les réductions d'impôts adoptées l'année dernière par les républicains, qui sont désormais confrontés au défi de conserver le contrôle du Congrès. Les ministres des Finances du G20 doivent se réunir jeudi en marge des réunions de Bangkok. Washington a profité de sa présidence du forum pour tenter de convaincre ses partenaires d'adopter des mesures plus fermes visant à contrer les politiques économiques de Pékin, qui ont entraîné une surcapacité industrielle et un afflux massif d'exportations chinoises à l'échelle mondiale. "Les pays excédentaires doivent augmenter leur consommation intérieure. Cela s'applique clairement au modèle de croissance de la Chine. Il faut passer d'une économie davantage axée sur les exportations à une économie davantage axée sur la consommation intérieure", a déclaré Kristalina Georgieva devant les journalistes. "Pour le dire très simplement, la Chine doit dépenser davantage, les États-Unis doivent épargner davantage et l'Europe doit investir davantage", a-t-elle ajouté. Le FMI estime dans ses [USN:L6N45Z04M TEXT:"dernières prévisions"] que l'économie mondiale parviendra à enregistrer une croissance supérieure à 3% en 2026 grâce aux investissements dans l'IA, qui compensent le choc énergétique provoqué par la guerre au Moyen-Orient, tout en méttant en garde contre des risques liés à une vague de ventes dans la technologie, la hausse des rendements de la dette souveraine ou les cyberattaques.

item.title: Galderma to buy US firm ZO Skin Health for $1.5 billion
item.description: Swiss skincare firm Galderma said on Wednesday it had agreed to acquire US-based company ZO Skin Health for an enterprise value of $1.5 billion, confirming a report published by Reuters earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss skincare firm Galderma (GALD.S) said on Wednesday it had agreed to acquire US-based company ZO Skin Health for an enterprise value of $1.5 billion, confirming a report published by Reuters [USN:L6N45Z1AR TEXT:"earlier in the day"]. • The acquisition brings together two complementary, science-backed skincare brands, ZO Skin Health and Galderma's Alastin • Galderma said the deal would expand its dermatological skincare offering in fast-growing, physician-dispensed skincare and support ZO Skin Health's next phase of growth. • The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 or early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. • The Swiss company said the acquisition of 100% of ZO Skin Health is expected to be neutral to core earnings per share in the first full year after the transaction closes. • Irvine, California-based ZO Skin Health has operated in professional skincare for more than 20 years. • ZO Skin Health logged net sales of around $330 million in the twelve months leading up to June 2026.

item.title: PSG boss Luis Enrique hopes Man City are not stripped of titles
item.description: The Paris St Germain boss said Manchester City should be allowed to keep their trophies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain boss Luis Enrique said Manchester City were deserving winners of their trophies and should be allowed to keep them, despite the English club facing sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The Premier League said City had used [USN:L6N45L10S TEXT:""sham" commercial contracts"] as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion). City, who have denied wrongdoing throughout the case and have [USN:L1N45O0BQ TEXT:"appealed the verdict"], could face punishments ranging from fines and a points deduction, to relegation and potentially being stripped of their titles. Asked about the verdict before PSG's Champions League match against City, Luis Enrique told a press conference on Tuesday: "The first thing when you hear that, it's a surprise, but I think we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision. "There are authorities responsible for making that decision, these decisions, and we have to wait, but if I speak only about football and the things that I saw on the pitch, Man City deserve those trophies. "I love the way they play football, and after that, you have to wait (for the) last decision and nothing else ... I think the trophies that you win on the pitch remains on the pitch, and they deserve to win that. I hope they can avoid that sanction." City host PSG at the Etihad Stadium later on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7535 pounds)

item.title: Trump says 'massive' oil, gas and mineral exploration to begin in Greenland
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive" oil, gas and mineral exploration is getting ready to begin in Greenland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive" oil, gas and mineral exploration is getting ready to begin in Greenland. Trump did not share details about the exploration plans in Greenland but said, "there are experts that are saying that the amount of easily available oil is far greater than that of almost any land, anywhere in the world." The United States, Denmark and Greenland last month [USN:L6N45E07X TEXT:"signed"] an agreement, aimed at ending tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island. "Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our Defense will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived," Trump added in his post on Truth Social. The deal signed between the US, Denmark and Greenland expands the [USN:L1N45D0X6 TEXT:"US military's role"] in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

item.title: Russian strikes kill three, damage dozens of power facilities
item.description: The hours-long missile and drone attack primarily targeted Kyiv and Kharkiv, and damaged 30 energy facilities, Zelenskiy said. At least 600,000 people were left without power.
item.dc:creator: Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: Russian strikes killed three people in Kyiv and plunged hundreds of thousands into darkness overnight, authorities said on Wednesday, in an attack President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called "ostentatious disrespect" to Donald Trump's peace effort. The hours-long missile and drone attack primarily targeted Kyiv and Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, and damaged 30 energy facilities, Zelenskiy said. At least 600,000 people were left without power, he added. US President Trump, who lifted sanctions on Russian diesel last week in a bid to lower politically sensitive fuel prices, has said that both sides agreed to halt strikes on energy infrastructure, though neither Moscow nor Kyiv confirmed it. "The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale – Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States," Zelenskiy wrote on X. "Russia does not consider the American President's statements strong." Russia's defence ministry said on Wednesday it had struck four power plants in and around Kyiv and two in Kharkiv, among other targets. LOW MISSILE INTERCEPTION RATE Ukraine reported downing just four out of 39 missiles, reflecting Kyiv's weakened air-defences against fast-moving ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones amid a shortage of weapons. Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian cities ahead of winter as it struggles on the battlefield, sparking fears of widespread power and heating outages across the country. Ukraine, for its part, has increasingly been attacking Russian oil refineries and logistics hubs in recent months, in what it views as one of the few ways it can respond to more than four and a half years of Russian bombardment. Wednesday's Russian attacks also targeted state railway facilities in five regions across Ukraine, said Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi. Trump blames Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries for the rise in fuel costs, especially of diesel, which has hit record prices since his war against Iran disrupted global oil supplies. Sources have told Reuters and other news organisations that the US threatened to cut off intelligence used for early warning of missile strikes on Ukraine unless Kyiv stops attacking Russian oil refineries. Zelenskiy had earlier said Ukraine had received no warning from Western partners before a previous overnight attack on the capital. Trump said on Tuesday that Washington was still sharing intelligence.

item.title: US to drop South Korea intelligence case against ex-CIA analyst
item.description: The US Justice Department has agreed to forgo prosecution of a former CIA analyst and White House National Security Council official who was accused of working as an unregistered agent for South Korea in exchange for luxury goods and other gifts.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department has agreed to forgo prosecution of a former CIA analyst and White House National Security Council official who was accused of working as an unregistered agent for South Korea in exchange for luxury goods and other gifts. Under a deferred prosecution deal reached with foreign policy specialist Sue Mi Terry, the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York said it would suspend criminal charges in the [USN:L1N3J80YP TEXT:"grand jury indictment"] returned against her in July 2024. Provided that Terry abides by several conditions stipulated in the deal, including restrictions on her travel and contacts with the government of South Korea, the case against her would be dropped altogether after 12 months of compliance. Terms of the agreement were laid out in a four-page deferred prosecution notice filed in US District Court in Manhattan on Tuesday. It gave Terry no explanation for why the Justice Department was essentially giving up its high-profile intelligence case except to say it had determined "that the interests of the United States and your own interest will be best served by deferring prosecution." The indictment accused Terry of accepting gifts from South Korea's government in return for advocating Seoul's policy positions, disclosing non-public information to its intelligence officers and facilitating access for South Korean government officials to their US counterparts. Her alleged work on behalf of South Korea as an unregistered foreign agent began in 2013, two years after she left US government employment, and ran for 10 years, including her time as a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations think tank. At the council, which placed her on unpaid leave following the indictment, she had worked as an expert on East Asia and Korean Peninsula. The indictment charged Terry with failing to register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, and conspiring to violate that law. Terry has maintained her innocence. Her lawyer, Lee Wolosky, said at the time that his client had been a harsh critic of the Seoul government and that she was being prosecuted for performing the work of an independent scholar and news analyst. The unexpected outcome spares Terry the immediate threat of a criminal conviction or any jail time. It comes weeks before the case was set to go to trial, according to the New York Times. "We have consistently maintained that her interactions with South Korean officials were conducted in furtherance of US interests and her work as a leading American specialist on North Korea and East Asia," the Times quoted Wolosky as saying in a statement about the agreement. As part of the deal, Terry admitted to no wrongdoing. But she acknowledged assisting South Korean intelligence officers in a number of ways, including sharing with them notes she had prepared for a meeting in 2022 between top State Department officials and Korea policy experts. She also admitted accepting designer handbags valued at more than $9,200, 19 meals at fine restaurants and $37,000 in payments to a public policy program on Korean affairs that she ran, as gifts from South Korean intelligence officers. Born in Seoul and raised in Virginia, Terry was a senior CIA analyst from 2001 to 2008, and director of Korean, Japan and Oceanic Affairs at the NSC from 2008 to 2009 under Republican President George W. Bush and Democratic President Barack Obama.

item.title: IMF calls for US to cut deficits amid bond woes, China to shift away from exports
item.description: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt without tax or spending adjustments, while China must pivot from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt without tax or spending adjustments, while China must pivot from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday. Georgieva admonished the world's two largest economies to make painful policy changes to reduce growing fiscal and trade imbalances, as her fiscal affairs chief said inflation, high debt levels and rising yields had heightened the urgency for fiscal consolidation around the globe. Speaking at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Georgieva singled out advanced economies, namely the US and European countries, as the "worst offenders" on excessive debts, with higher benchmark yields spilling over to low-income countries that have already been forced by financial markets to rein in debts. Asked at a press conference whether the US needs tighter fiscal policy, Georgieva said US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recognizes that US deficit and debt levels are too high and need to be made more sustainable. "The authorities very much rely on strong growth in the United States" to help reduce debt, Georgieva said. "At the Fund, we believe that growth of course helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments. So, some (fiscal) measures would be necessary." The call for more action to reduce debt was echoed in the IMF's [USN:L1N460042 TEXT:"Fiscal Monitor"] report on Wednesday, which warned that delays in an era of higher borrowing costs would only make the job harder in coming years. While that message is a perennial one from the IMF, Rodrigo Valdes, the head of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs department, said the surge in bond yields had left governments with little fiscal room to manoeuvre. "We dialled up the urgency of our message," he added. BESSENT NO-SHOW Bessent is not attending the annual meetings in Bangkok, despite this year's US presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, instead favouring domestic engagements as the US midterm election campaign heats up. He has acted as a chief spokesman for President Donald Trump's economic policies, particularly touting the deep tax cuts passed last year by Republicans now trying to maintain control of the US Congress. G20 finance ministers are due to meet on the sidelines of the Bangkok meetings on Thursday. The US has used its G20 presidency to try to rally allies to take stronger action to counter China's [USN:L1N44T0JC TEXT:""non-market" economic policies"] that have led to [USN:L1N45T0MB TEXT:"excess industrial capacity"] and a flood of global exports. Asked about imbalances emanating from China, on a day when data showed it was on track to post a[USN:L6N46005Q TEXT:" record trade surplus"], Georgieva repeated longstanding advice to Beijing: "For surplus countries, what they need to do is increase domestic consumption. That clearly applies to China's growth model. Shift from export more toward domestic consumption." Deficit countries need to save more and spend less, while Europe needs to invest more in competitiveness, she said. "To put it very simply, China needs to spend more, the US has to save more, and Europe has to invest more," Georgieva added. CALL FOR AID TO POOR COUNTRIES This week's meetings have been dominated by worries about growing debt and rising bond yields and risks from the artificial intelligence boom. Regarding the growing divergence between advanced countries benefiting from AI investment and those bypassed by it, highlighted in Tuesday's IMF [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"economic forecasts"], Georgieva also urged IMF member countries to [USN:L1N46004N TEXT:"fully fund"] IMF facilities for low-income and vulnerable countries. These include the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which provides low- and zero-interest loans to low-income countries, and the Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust, a fund that provides grants for debt-service relief and cancellation to the poorest and most vulnerable member countries, she said. These countries, too, were being squeezed by higher bond yields, with average debt service costs that have increased to 14% of revenue from 6% a decade ago, even as overall debt burdens have eased, she said. "The risk of divergence is most dangerous for those that are already further behind," Georgieva added.

item.title: US Justice Department threatens California over alleged noncitizen voters, letter shows
item.description: It gave California officials 48 hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage , Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Tuesday gave California officials 48 hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters - part of an unprecedented effort to find evidence of voter fraud ahead of next month's elections. The letter, written by acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter and addressed to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber, says the Justice Department provided officials in Los Angeles County with a "password-protected thumb drive" with the names of people the federal government "believes are likely noncitizens" and were sent mail-in ballots. The letter demands that the state refuse to send ballots to those on the list until their citizenship status has been confirmed. Voters in question who have already received ballots should have their ballot "segregated" once it is mailed back; ballots already returned should not be tabulated "until citizenship has been determined," the letter stipulates. The federal government "will have no choice but to seek emergency relief," according to the letter, if state officials do not follow its instructions. "Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes," McCotter wrote. The letter marks an escalation of the Trump administration's attempts to pressure states over alleged voting by non-US citizens and signals the Justice Department may be prepared to challenge ballots in the weeks leading up to the November 3 election, when Republicans will be defending their narrow majorities in Congress. Justice Department spokeswoman Kiersten Pels confirmed the existence of the letter in a statement to Reuters, adding: "The department will take all necessary legal action to protect election integrity and ensure compliance with federal law.” Representatives from the White House and the California secretary of state's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. FRAUD CLAIMS The Justice Department under President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed that voting by non-US citizens is widespread, despite multiple studies showing it is rare. Though states may have added more than [USN:L6N43Z058 TEXT:"30,000 noncitizens to their voter rolls"] since 2000 due to software glitches and clerical errors, Reuters found in September, it was unclear how many had cast a ballot. Experts said the numbers were too small relative to the country’s 170 million registered voters to affect elections. In July, the Justice Department [USN:L6N43A182 TEXT:"sent letters"] to chief election officials in all 50 states warning they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls or cast ballots. The department's Civil Rights Division has demanded nonpublic voter data, including voters' Social Security numbers or dates of birth, from nearly all states as part of its hunt for noncitizens on state rolls. It has [USN:L6N44118V TEXT:"sued"] 30 Democratic- and Republican-led states that refused to hand over their rolls, but has [USN:S0N3R907R TEXT:"lost 26 of those cases"] without winning one. Reuters [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"reported"] last month that the Department of Homeland Security was using a commercial data broker to find sensitive voter information not included in publicly available rolls, which officials and experts warned could lead to citizens being falsely flagged as illegal voters and potentially detained. Federal prosecutors have also [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"ramped up"] prosecutions of noncitizens for allegedly voting in past elections or submitting fraudulent registrations, touting 16 new criminal cases on Monday. Officials in Democratic-led California have tussled for months with the Trump administration over its attempts to intervene in election procedures over allegations of voter fraud. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin informed California officials on July 16 that the federal government believed the state had noncitizens on its voting rolls, according to the letter. California could prove pivotal in deciding control of the US House of Representatives, especially after the state's voters approved a new congressional map that heavily favors Democrats as part of a nationwide redistricting sprint that began in Republican-led states. Voters in Los Angeles will also weigh in on a ballot measure that would allow certain noncitizen legal residents to cast ballots in municipal elections.

item.title: Singapore marine fuel supplier Equatorial eyes higher LNG bunker demand from 2028
item.description: Equatorial Marine Fuel Management, a top Singapore bunker supplier by volume, plans to channel part of its 2026 profits to fund its expansion into supplying liquefied natural gas to ships as it positions for higher demand from 2028, its executives said.
item.dc:creator: Jeslyn Lerh
item.content:encoded: Equatorial Marine Fuel Management, a top Singapore bunker supplier by volume, plans to channel part of its 2026 profits to fund its expansion into supplying liquefied natural gas to ships as it positions for higher demand from 2028, its executives said. The company, which was one of eight suppliers [USN:L1N43W0ED TEXT:"awarded"] an LNG bunker licence in late July, is in discussions with LNG cargo suppliers and shipowners for collaborations, its executive director Choong Zhen Mao told Reuters on the sidelines of the Singapore International Bunkering conference (SIBCON) 2026. "The opportunity that we see in LNG still seems to be growing, even in this climate. I think that's where we see the market moving," he said, referring to the surge in LNG prices after the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted exports from the Middle East. The company will be receiving its first new-built LNG bunker barge in the later part of the third quarter in 2027, he added. Singapore's January-to-September 2026 LNG bunker sales totalled 487,100 tons, up more than 21% from a year earlier, data from the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore showed Wednesday. Equatorial's chief operating officer, Choong Sheen Mao, expects a more notable increase in Singapore's LNG bunker demand from 2028 as more LNG production capacity and dual-fuel vessels come online globally. Equatorial currently supplies about 10% of total bunker volumes at Singapore, the world's biggest refuelling hub for ships, according to its executives. The city state has supplied an average 4.7 million tons of bunker fuel a month so far in 2026, official data show. The company's year-to-date profits for 2026 have exceeded last year's level, the executives said, though they did not disclose the figures. Bunker fuel prices surged after US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February drove oil prices higher, and have remained volatile since then. The ensuing disruption to shipping routes supported refuelling demand in key hubs including Singapore. "Demand looks to be resilient," said ED Choong. "When there is uncertainty, sometimes people tend to purchase a bit more, fill their tanks a bit more... people tend to break a voyage down into smaller trades these days to ensure availability and cargo security." Equatorial owns eight fuel oil barges, seven marine gasoil barges, as well as four chemical bunker tankers that meet International Maritime Organization's type 2 standard to carry methanol or biofuel blends up to 100% biofuel content. Some of the chemical bunker tankers have been repurposed to supply conventional fuel this year amid a slowdown in marine biofuel demand, COO Choong said. "Demand for biofuels has slowed this year because of the delay in the IMO's net-zero framework, while current prices are not competitive," he said. Depending on the blend and delivery window, biofuel blends command premiums of at least $100 per metric ton over conventional low-sulphur bunker fuel oil, according to industry sources.

item.title: Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW, Politico amid legal fight
item.description: A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them, in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute.
item.dc:creator: Jack Queen, Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them, in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute. US District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a written decision that elaborated on his September 24 emergency order that reinstated access for the journalists. The news organizations and press freedom groups have accused Trump of unconstitutional retaliation against journalists for coverage he does not like. Kelly's order last month gave the CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists access to the White House grounds on a temporary basis. The judge issued a ruling called a preliminary injunction on Tuesday that will remain in effect until he makes a final judgment in the lawsuit brought by the news organizations, unless an appeals court lifts his order. Kelly wrote that Trump's public remarks made clear that he banned the news outlets because he considered their reporting biased and inaccurate, and not because of national security concerns as government lawyers later asserted in court. "Simply put, that is unlawful viewpoint discrimination," the judge wrote, adding that "no one should read this decision as suggesting that President Trump’s complaints are meritless." Trump appointed Kelly in 2017 during his first presidential term. CAMPAIGN AGAINST THE MEDIA Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organizations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets. Trump announced the ban in September on his social media platform, saying CNN, Politico, and MS NOW "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." The Justice Department has emphasized Trump's contention that the ban is legally justified on national security grounds. The outlets have said the revocation of their White House passes was unlawful retaliation for their news coverage and accused the Trump administration of manufacturing meritless national security concerns to justify the ban. The outlets said in a lawsuit that the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for freedom of speech and a free press, as well as their rights to due process, meaning fair treatment from the government. The White House on September 24 reinstated the CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists after Kelly decided the ban "likely violated their constitutional due process rights," and ordered their access immediately restored. 'COERCE BETTER COVERAGE' The judge held a hearing on October 8 to hear arguments by the news outlets and the Justice Department over whether to extend the protection for the journalists against being barred from the White House. The Justice Department defended the bans as fair and justified. "Here we have the unusual situation where the president himself has said he wants to chill speech. He wants to coerce better coverage," Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the outlets, told Kelly during the hearing. "CNN, MS NOW and Politico engaged in apparently indefensible conduct," Justice Department lawyer Michael Velchik said. The legal battle is being waged just weeks before the November 3 US midterm elections in which Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress. Trump's job approval ratings are at record lows in opinion polls amid concerns over issues such as inflation and the Iran war.

item.title: Gold down for third straight session as markets await US inflation data
item.description: Gold edged lower for a third straight session on Wednesday as oil prices climbed, while investors turned their attention to incoming US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next policy move.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold edged lower for a third straight session on Wednesday as oil prices climbed, while investors turned their attention to incoming US inflation data for clues on the Federal Reserve's next policy move. Spot gold dipped 0.3% to $4,142.85 per ounce by 0924 GMT. U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 0.3% to $4,165.40 per ounce. "I think for a large part, a lot of traders are sitting on their hands ahead of the release of the CPI data later today, which could impact the direction of the US dollar, gold prices and everything else really pricing the dollar," said Fawad Razaqzada, market analyst at Forex.com. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is due at 1230 GMT, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data on Thursday. Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, as Tehran seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections. "Once the US dollar pops out, we are very close to seeing the dollar potentially topping out. That's when gold is going to shine more brightly. I reckon that the metal could rise back towards the 4,500 area, 4,700 even in the later months of the year," Razaqzada added. While gold is typically seen as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates tend to diminish the appeal of non-yielding bullion. New York Fed President [USN:L6N45Z14X TEXT:"John Williams"] reaffirmed his view that the US central bank may need to raise rates once more this year in its bid to lower inflation. Markets see about a 22% chance of a US rate hike this month and a 90% probability of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Among other metals, spot silver fell 1.6% to $58.5161 per ounce, platinum dipped 0.8% to $1,649.93 per ounce and palladium was little changed at $1,124.93 per ounce.

item.title: Rupee extends rise but falters past 95/USD on importer hedging, outflows
item.description: The Indian rupee rose for a third consecutive session on Wednesday to hit a more than one-month peak as the central bank followed up tough regulatory measures with hawkish commentary.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee rose for a third consecutive session on Wednesday to hit a more than one-month peak as the central bank followed up tough regulatory measures with hawkish commentary. However, the gains were capped below the 95 per dollar mark as dollar demand linked to importer hedging and portfolio outflows persisted. The rupee climbed to a peak of 94.77 in early trading before settling 0.1% higher at 95.15. "A durable turnaround in the currency will also require negative global triggers to subside. The latest announcements may not fully quell speculation over further policy action," DBS said in a note. "Should depreciation pressures intensify again, markets are likely to price a higher probability of a front-loaded and more aggressive rate-hike cycle." Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra has defended India's recent forex curbs as an effort to discourage speculative bets and said the central bank is ready to take additional steps to ensure orderly rupee movement. He added that while monetary policy is not typically deployed to address financial stability concerns, the two cannot be entirely separated. Traders interpreted the remarks as a signal of limited tolerance to further rupee weakness. The South Asian currency had declined over 7% year-to-date before fresh measures over the weekend and has risen 2% this week. Rupee swap markets are currently pricing in nearly 100 bps of rate hikes over the next 12 months. Indian importers [USN:L1N46009M TEXT:"continue to lock in"] future dollar purchase rates to protect against the rupee weakening, despite the banks charging more following the central bank's steps. Investors await US consumer inflation data, due later in the day, for cues on the future path of interest rates in the world's largest economy. The dollar index was last at 102.2.

item.title: China's September exports soar, putting $1 trillion trade surplus in sight
item.description: China's trade surplus widened more than expected in September as exports surged, keeping the country on track to surpass last year's record surplus and likely intensifying trade tensions with major partners.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Zhang, Ellen Zhang, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: China's trade surplus widened more than expected in September as exports surged, keeping the country on track to surpass last year's record surplus and likely intensifying trade tensions with major partners. Global demand for semiconductors and green-tech products has helped keep China's factories humming, easing pressure on policymakers to shore up economic growth against subdued domestic demand and investment. Exports soared 36.3% from a year earlier, outstripping August's 25.0% rise and far exceeding expectations for 25.5% growth, customs data showed on Wednesday. September's growth was the fastest since February when exports expanded 39.6%. Imports also remained robust, up 31.0% compared with 28.2% growth in August and economists' forecasts of a 24.5% gain. Wang Jun, a vice customs minister, told a press briefing there would be external uncertainties including geopolitical conflicts that might affect trade, but added there was foundation and support for continued growth in exports and imports in the fourth quarter. Analysts expect trade to remain buoyant, with tech products continuing to drive exports and imports. "Key trade ties look set to remain stable through year-end, which should keep this year's key growth engine humming," said Lynn Song, ING's chief Greater China economist. China's yuan held steady against the dollar on Wednesday, underpinned by solid exports data, while stocks (.CSI300) fell. RISING TRADE SURPLUS China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion in November last year and posted a record $1.189 trillion for the whole year. The surplus reached $938.11 billion in the first nine months of this year, putting the manufacturing powerhouse on course to hit the $1 trillion mark sooner unless exports slow sharply in the final quarter. For now, such a slowdown appears unlikely. September's trade surplus widened to $133.53 billion, helped by a 20-month-high $34.01 billion surplus with the United States and a larger $34.8 billion surplus with the European Union. A [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"deal"] with the EU to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc, announced earlier this month, is likely to weigh on China's booming auto trade over time. But with the trade measures likely being laid out in [USN:L6N45Y0JN TEXT:"December"], exporters may drive up shipments to beat the deadline. "The widening trade surplus with Europe could spur broader EU restrictions beyond last week's narrow deal, though we expect the resulting economic fallout for China to be small," said Capital Economics's China economist Nguyen Hoang Nam. President Xi Jinping's September summit with US President Donald Trump in Washington secured an [USN:L1N45F0IM TEXT:"extension"] to their tariff truce and an agreement to [USN:L6N45K03P TEXT:"cut tariffs"] on $30 billion worth of goods from each side. High-tech goods and cars continued to underpin shipments, with semiconductor exports rising 108.1% year-on-year in value terms in the first nine months. Auto exports expanded more than 50% in both value and volume terms. With the global build-out of AI infrastructure showing little sign of slowing, analysts expect demand for Chinese-made technology products, including semiconductors, to remain robust. China's [USN:L1N460014 TEXT:"factory-gate prices"] rose at their fastest pace in more than four years in September, separate data showed, while consumer inflation edged up but lagged forecasts, underscoring an uneven recovery. The Canton Fair, China's largest trade exhibition, kicks off on Thursday for Chinese manufacturers to showcase their products to foreign buyers. In commodities, September crude oil imports [USN:L4N4600AD TEXT:"fell"] 21.5% year-on-year in volume terms, while soybean imports were down 7.7% from the same month last year. RISKS LOOM The strength in exports indicates that policymakers could still rely on moderate policy support to meet China's 4.5% to 5% annual GDP growth target. Risks of curbs on Chinese exports loom as China continues to defend its industrial and monetary policies, which Washington and Brussels blame for Beijing's massive trade surplus. China's central bank last week [USN:L6N45U0ON TEXT:"pushed back"] against criticism of its exchange-rate policy with a lengthy statement, arguing that it never pursued competitive depreciation and rejecting claims that China keeps the yuan artificially weak to gain a trade advantage. Any major hit to exports, a key growth engine, could prompt policymakers to step up stimulus measures to address weak domestic demand and the years-long property market downturn.

item.title: Indian shares end lower as higher oil prices, foreign outflows dent appetite
item.description: Indian shares closed lower on Wednesday as firmer oil prices and sustained foreign outflows weighed on risk sentiment after a rebound in the previous session, while investors assessed earnings and awaited key US inflation data.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran
item.content:encoded: Indian shares closed lower on Wednesday as firmer oil prices and sustained foreign outflows weighed on risk sentiment after a rebound in the previous session, while investors assessed earnings and awaited key US inflation data. The Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.44% to 22,622.70, while the BSE Sensex (.BSESN) dipped 0.34% to 72,781.89. Eight of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) fell 0.3% and 0.1%, respectively. The Nifty and Sensex climbed about 1.6% each on [USN:L4N45Z0KR TEXT:"Tuesday"], led by information technology stocks after HCLTech's (HCLT.NS) [USN:L6N45Z08A TEXT:"quarterly profit"] beat expectations. IT index (.NIFTYIT) , which gained 5.2% in the previous session, added 1.1% on the day. Oil prices rose to $106 a barrel after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, heightening supply concerns, while Iranian officials said they were deploying new tactics to target ships. "Going forward, the direction of markets will depend on a combination of global risk appetite, currency movements, crude oil prices and corporate earnings momentum," Vinit Bolinjkar, head of research at Ventura said, adding that markets may remain highly volatile and selective in the near term. Investors now await a key US inflation data due later in the day for clues on the Federal Reserve's rate trajectory. Higher US rates tend to reduce the appeal of emerging markets such as India to overseas investors. Foreign portfolio investors extended their selling streak to 13 sessions on Tuesday, taking year-to-date outflows to a record $32.52 billion. "While domestic institutional participation remains the source of market resilience, that alone may not be sufficient to sustain a broad-based rally if foreign outflows persist," Ventura's Bolinjkar said. Among individual stocks, Tata Elxsi (TTEX.NS) climbed 5.7% after the engineering research and development firm [USN:L4N45Z17R TEXT:"posted"] higher quarterly profit. Bank of Baroda (BOB.NS) fell 4% after UAE-based businessman BR Shetty, founder of NMC Healthcare, filed a $15 billion lawsuit against the state-owned lender and 25 other defendants in the Bombay High Court.

item.title: SK Group Chairman Chey sells stake to Dell family office fund for $406 million
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million), a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc (034730.KS) to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million), a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday. The deal is part of Chey's plan to raise 944 billion won through share sales to pay a divorce settlement to his former wife. Here are some details: The buyer of 972,493 SK Inc shares was identified as DFO Public Investments, L.P., a Delaware-based investment fund affiliated with DFO Management, the family investment office of Michael Dell, according to the filing and DFO Management's website. Earlier this month, SK Inc said in a filing that Chey had agreed to [USN:L1N45O06F TEXT:"sell 1.65 million shares, or a 2.26% stake"] for 944 billion won. Of those, 681,431 shares, or 0.94%, will be sold to Korea Investment & Securities for 400 billion won. SK had previously identified the buyer of the remaining shares only as a strategic investor, saying the investor had agreed to buy the stake after considering SK Inc's business competitiveness and medium- to long-term growth prospects. Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data centre infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix (000660.KS) , SK Group's memory chipmaking unit. The stake is being acquired by a Dell family investment fund, rather than Dell Technologies itself. Reuters reported in May that global technology companies had approached SK Hynix with [USN:L4N41K05W TEXT:"proposals"] to invest in dedicated memory chip production lines and help finance costly manufacturing equipment as they sought to secure supplies amid booming AI demand. The Korea Corporate Governance Forum said Chey and the buyers would be required to disclose their stakes as joint holdings if they had agreed, even informally, to exercise their voting rights in the same way. Failure to do so would violate South Korea's capital markets law, it said. The forum, an independent watchdog that monitors corporate governance issues in South Korea, said a strategic investor suggested their interests could be aligned, raising the possibility that the fund could be deemed a joint holder with Chey under the law. ($1 = 1,339.6000 won)

item.title: Oil prices rise as Iran deploys new tactics to target tankers
item.description: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday after an attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, while Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly
item.content:encoded: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday after an attack on the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, while Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"new tactics"] to target ships, seeking to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections. Brent crude futures were up 14 cents to $105.83 a barrel at 0938 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 57 cents to $94.71. Both contracts had climbed more than $1 in early trade, with WTI hitting a more than two-week high at $95.41 a barrel. "Attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz and military strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are supporting prices as market participants remain concerned about lower oil exports from the region," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that exports have held up so far. Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy to target ships, but one said that Iran had started to use different offensive tactics about 10 days ago. "That Iranian officials are openly admitting to undermining US efforts to keep oil prices under control speaks volumes about the real intentions behind the so-called 'peace talks'," said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova. ATTACKS ON MULTIPLE FRONTS The Iran-allied Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday. The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"international airport"] has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people. Meanwhile, a container ship [USN:S8N43Z00E TEXT:"sank "]in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine and catching fire, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement shared by state media on Wednesday. This comes a day after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a container ship and a tanker were hit by unknown projectiles within the strait. "The expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment. US President Donald Trump announced last Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine . Russia's crude oil [USN:L1N46008R TEXT:"production increased"] by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd but remained 870,000 bpd down year on year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday. The IEA also said that a lack of operational Russian refinery capacity meant that the recently announced easing of Russian diesel export restrictions was unlikely to bring any material change to the global gasoil market balance. Constrained diesel supplies could persist well into next year, the IEA also said.

item.title: Dollar eases as investors await CPI data, Fed speakers
item.description: The dollar fell further from 18-month highs against the euro on Wednesday as investors awaited US inflation data and comments from Federal Reserve policymakers for fresh clues on the pace of monetary policy tightening.
item.dc:creator: Rocky Swift, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: The dollar fell further from 18-month highs against the euro on Wednesday as investors awaited US inflation data and comments from Federal Reserve policymakers for fresh clues on the pace of monetary policy tightening. The euro edged higher as European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"dashed expectations"] of intervention to prop up France's battered bond market, though Brent crude at $106 a barrel put a lid on the currency's rise. Attention is now on the release of US consumer price index data, as well as speeches from Fed officials that could clarify the outlook for interest rates. Economists polled by Reuters expect the price index to have risen 0.6% month-on-month in September after increasing 0.4% in August, while annual inflation is seen accelerating to 3.6% from 3.4%. "The risk is that US CPI hits 4% or that the core picks up as well. This would spark higher yields and a firmer dollar, with the euro being further battered below this week’s low of $1.1152," said Roberto Mialich, FX strategist at Unicredit. The dollar index , which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies, fell 0.05% to 102.15, as Treasury yields ticked lower. The dollar had also fallen on Tuesday after comments that were interpreted as dovish from New York Fed President John Williams and Fed Governor Christopher Waller. "I don't think at this time I have any reason to believe that we would need to do more," Williams told Bloomberg News in an [USN:L6N45Z14X TEXT:"interview"], referring to the possibility of further rate hikes in 2027. Traders see a 78% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago, while pricing in about 79 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The US central bank raised its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Fed officials Thomas Barkin and Michelle Bowman are due to speak later on Wednesday. Additionally, the Fed publishes its monthly Beige Book. EURO TROUBLES A host of global finance chiefs are in Bangkok, where the International Monetary Fund and World Bank are holding annual meetings. IMF fiscal affairs chief Rodrigo Valdes said the body has "dialed up" the urgency of its call for governments to rein in growing debts, while the IMF's Kristalina Georgieva said the US needs to make fiscal [USN:S0N40K04E TEXT:"adjustments"] to put its debt on a more sustainable path. French bonds have been among the worst hit by a recent global selloff, with investors concerned that political jostling ahead of next year's presidential election may hinder efforts to reduce its high deficit. The ECB's Lagarde said at a CNN event in Bangkok that France should [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"solve"] its debt woes through fiscal consolidation, damping speculation about whether the central bank might start buying French bonds to contain yields. The euro was up 0.06% at $1.1205, having touched a fresh 17-month low against the dollar this week, as soaring French borrowing costs added to inflation concerns driven by higher energy costs. "In the near term, I cannot rule out the risk that the euro might test to $1.10. Going towards the end of the year, we're less bearish. Our take is that bond yield in the US will probably ease although the situation in the euro zone could weigh on the euro," said Unicredit's Mialich. The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that British finance minister John Healey is expected to pay for all new giveaways in this month’s budget with higher taxes or spending cuts rather than more [USN:FWN45Z1XZ TEXT:"borrowing."] The IMF is not recommending that Britain speed up its fiscal [USN:L1N460035 TEXT:"consolidation"], a senior official of the body said. Sterling strengthened 0.08% to $1.3265. The Japanese yen inched up 0.03% to 158.395 per dollar.

item.title: Aluminium's calm belies lingering supply-chain stress
item.description: Iranian missile attacks on Gulf smelters and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz have knocked out almost 3 million metric tons of aluminium production capacity. Yet, eight months on, the market is seemingly unconcerned.
item.dc:creator: Andy Home
item.content:encoded: Iranian missile attacks on Gulf smelters and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz have knocked out almost 3 million metric tons of [USN:L8N43P15H TEXT:"aluminium production"] capacity. Yet, eight months on, the market is seemingly unconcerned. Indeed, London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month aluminium is now trading just above $3,000 per ton, which is where it was in early February before the US and Israel unleashed Operation Epic Fury against Iran. Traders are betting that a combination of rising output in Indonesia and higher product exports from China can tide things over until the Gulf smelters are repaired and shipping fully resumes in the Strait of Hormuz. The surface calm, however, masks lingering stress in a physical supply chain that is still reeling from the unprecedented disruption. PLUGGING THE GAPS Gulf production of primary aluminium slumped by an annualized 2.8 million tons between February and May, according to the International Aluminium Institute. The collapse reflected the forced shutdown of Emirates Global Aluminium's Al-Taweelah smelter and damage to Aluminium Bahrain's (ALBH.BH) facility, as well as logistics problems at other Gulf operators. Regional production has since been creeping higher as both plants [USN:L1N44907E TEXT:"undergo repairs"] and ramp production back up, but the August run-rate of 3.5 million tons annualised was still 2.6 million tons below pre-hostility levels. China and Indonesia have stepped in to plug the gap. China's exports of primary metal are constrained by a hefty 30% export duty, but outbound volumes of alloy doubled year-on-year to 349,000 tons in the January to August period. Exports of semi-finished products such as aluminium plate, sheet and strip surged by 774,000 tons to 4.46 million tons over the same period. Indonesia's [USN:L8N44Z0XJ TEXT:"new"] Chinese-owned smelters are also ramping up at speed. The country exported 114,000 tons of primary metal in July, a fresh monthly record. Around half of last year's Indonesian aluminium exports went to China but shipments since the Iran war have been dispersed across Asia, Europe and even the US. PHYSICAL STRESS Improved availability in Asia has caused physical premiums to ease from their June highs. Japanese buyers have negotiated a fourth-quarter delivery premium of $255 per ton over the LME cash price, which marks a 35% decline from the previous quarter. However, that's still higher than the $200-per-ton premium that was trading at the start of the Iran war, attesting to continued tension even in this relatively well-supplied part of the market. European buyers are paying significantly more for their physical metal. The CME European duty-paid premium is trading at $559 per ton over LME cash, double the level at the end of February. US buyers, of course, are paying more than anyone else for their aluminium with the US Midwest premium trading at an elevated $2,312 per ton over LME cash, though this is as much about President Donald Trump's 50% [USN:S0N3RL03L TEXT:"import tariffs"] as anything else. LOW INVENTORY Elevated premiums are sucking available metal into the physical supply chain, leaving LME stocks at multi-year lows. Registered inventory of 238,625 tons is the lowest level this century. Most of what remains is Russian metal, which reduces its appeal to most Western buyers. LME off-warrant inventory has also been steadily shrinking since February and now totals just 73,509 tons, which is the lowest reading since the LME introduced this category of stocks reporting in 2020. Time-spreads have eased considerably since June, when the cash premium over three-month metal jumped to over $100 per ton. But there is lingering tightness in the front part of the curve. After a period of mild contango, cash has just returned to a small premium over three-month metal again. Time-spread tension is likely to remain a feature of the London market as long as physical premiums remain so high. The aluminium market has proved highly resilient to the sudden loss of so much production, but the stress lines are still there beneath the calm surface.
