item.title: Ukrainian ex-officer stands trial in Germany over Nord Stream bombing
item.description: A Ukrainian ex-military officer went on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray
item.content:encoded: A Ukrainian ex-military officer went on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas. The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert to mount one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case will provide the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the crime. Prosecutors have alleged that Serhii K., who was arrested under an international warrant in Italy last year, worked with members of the Ukrainian military to plan the [USN:L8N3UD0YM TEXT:"clandestine operation"] on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities. Serhii K. has denied any involvement in the blasts that ruptured the 1,200-km (750-mile)-long Baltic Sea pipeline. The government in Kyiv has also denied any involvement, a sensitive point in its relations with Germany, Ukraine's largest European supplier of military aid. The Russian government said on Monday it expected a "just verdict" that would reveal the names of the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation. ATTACKING CIVILIAN TARGETS IS CONSIDERED A WAR CRIME German prosecutors say the actions Serhii K. is accused of — attacking civilian targets and causing explosions that destroyed infrastructure and damaged public services — would amount to a war crime. The alleged aim was to disrupt a major source of foreign revenue for Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched earlier that year. Protesters gathered outside the Hamburg court in support of the defendant, with a sign that read: "What are war crimes?" "Russia is the only war criminal that belongs in the dock," said one of the dozens of protesters. He is the only person on trial, but Croatian authorities have [USN:L6N44H0T9 TEXT:"arrested"] another man, identified as Vladimir Z., who prosecutors believe was one of the [USN:SPN44900E TEXT:"divers"]. The explosion of Nord Stream sealed the end of Germany's longstanding dependence on Russian natural gas, although Moscow had already cut supplies over Berlin's support for European sanctions following Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Germany previously received half its natural gas imports through the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, by far the biggest and most modern Russian pipeline serving western Europe, which allowed Russia to bypass Soviet-era pipelines transiting Ukraine. The supply had been due to double with the opening of a twin pipeline, Nord Stream 2, already built although Berlin cancelled approval to open it just prior to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. PLUMES OF METHANE GAS The trial, expected to continue into February next year, could also have domestic political implications. Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), leading in opinion polls for more than a year, has called for an end to military aid for Ukraine and a restoration of energy ties with Moscow. In the initial months after the pipelines were attacked, Western officials mainly pointed fingers at Russia. Moscow has always denied any involvement and called the suggestion it would blow up its own pipelines absurd. It also rejects charges that it has more recently targeted Western infrastructure with so-called "hybrid" sabotage and drone attacks. The Nord Stream system, lying at a depth of 80 to 110 metres under the Baltic and built by Russian gas concern Gazprom to supply up to 110 billion cubic metres of gas to Germany, was formerly at the core of economic ties between the two countries. On September 26, 2022, several blasts, some 17 hours apart, were detected by Swedish seismologists. The blasts sent huge plumes of methane gas into the atmosphere as three of the four concrete-coated steel pipelines were ruptured. Prosecutors allege that Serhii K. travelled to Germany through Poland some three weeks before the attack, using a forged Ukrainian passport. They say he and his group used a sailboat hired in the northern German city of Rostock to reach an area close to the Danish island of Bornholm, where they rigged specialised military-grade explosives fitted with timers to the sea floor. The weekly Der Spiegel magazine and ZDF public television have previously reported that five men and one woman were on the rented yacht Andromeda, which left Rostock on September 6 and returned on September 23, 2022.

item.title: Russian missile attack on Kyiv kills two, Zelenskiy says no warning received
item.description: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian capital with ballistic missiles on Tuesday, killing two people in a high-rise apartment and hitting a thermal power plant in the second attack in 24 hours without warning from Kyiv's Western allies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian forces struck the Ukrainian capital with ballistic missiles on Tuesday, killing two people in a high-rise apartment and hitting a thermal power plant in the second attack in 24 hours without warning from Kyiv's Western allies. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said the main target was energy infrastructure. He said it was unfair that Kyiv was enduring attacks without warnings from partners and said intelligence showed that more strikes were likely. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the strike on the nine-storey building had killed two people and injured 21. Sixteen were being treated in hospital and four were in a serious condition. Emergency crews were battling fires in apartments throughout the building and residents were being evacuated. Reuters pictures and TV footage showed firefighters training hoses on the building's shattered facade. "Once again, no advance warning from our partners. The main target was energy infrastructure, specifically thermal plant No. 4," Zelenskiy said on Telegram. "According to our intelligence, the Russians are preparing further ballistic missile launches." "The facts show that the Russians do not consider themselves bound to abide by what the president of the United States said," he added, referring to US President Donald Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire at the weekend. "And it is certainly unfair that they are destroying our energy infrastructure while Ukraine is not even receiving warnings about ballistic missile launches." Zelenskiy had [USN:L1N45Z0GP TEXT:"earlier said"] that Ukraine had received no warning from Western partners before a previous overnight attack on the capital. Trump said Washington was still sharing intelligence even as he pressured Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries. Reuters and other media have reported that US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it stops attacking Russian refineries. Kyiv relies heavily on US intelligence for early warnings of missile strikes, experts and officials say.

item.title: Tresoldi treble stuns Inter, Bayern held as Barcelona rally
item.description: Nicolo Tresoldi's hat-trick powered Club Brugge to a stunning 4-3 Champions League victory at Inter Milan on a night of scares for Europe's heavyweights.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Nicolo Tresoldi's hat-trick powered Club Brugge to a stunning 4-3 Champions League victory at Inter Milan on a night of scares for Europe's heavyweights on Tuesday, with Bayern Munich held 3-3 at Viking Stavanger while Barcelona recovered to beat Galatasaray 4-1. Bayern fought back from two goals down to lead in Norway but Michael Olise's dismissal left them exposed and Herman Johan Haugen struck in added time to earn Viking a point. Barcelona proved more convincing in Istanbul, overturning a first-half deficit with Lamine Yamal supplying two assists, while Atletico Madrid won 2-0 against Manchester United, who had Leny Yoro sent off, and Arsenal scored three times in seven minutes to defeat Lille 3-0. TRESOLDI PUNISHES INTER Tresoldi, who had already hit the post, put Brugge ahead with a penalty on the half-hour mark after Hakan Calhanoglu fouled Carlos Forbs. Lautaro Martinez equalised before halftime, holding off his marker and turning to finish after Marcus Thuram and Federico Dimarco combined down the left. But a misunderstanding between Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez and his defence allowed Carlos Forbs to knock the ball through the keeper's legs, leaving Tresoldi to tap into an empty net and restore Brugge’s lead. Tresoldi completed his hat-trick in the 74th minute before Martinez's second goal seven minutes later revived Inter's hopes. Romeo Vermant made it 4-2 in the 87th minute, leaving Ange-Yoan Bonny's reply deep into added time as scant consolation for the home supporters. BAYERN DENIED LATE Gianni Stensness headed Viking ahead from a second-minute corner and the hosts doubled their advantage in the 38th with a sweeping counter-attack as Bayern pressed for an equaliser. Harry Kane began the comeback with a 54th-minute penalty following a lengthy VAR review of Kristoffer Haugen's foul on Konrad Laimer, then headed Bayern level six minutes later. Kane has now scored in nine successive Champions League matches, equalling the competition's second-longest scoring run, behind Cristiano Ronaldo's 11. Luis Diaz put Bayern ahead in the 71st minute, but Olise received his second yellow card three minutes later and Haugen's late equaliser denied the visitors victory. Barcelona also trailed after Alexey Batrakov scored for Galatasaray in the 28th minute. The hosts thought they had doubled their lead through a Baris Yilmaz header, only for VAR to identify an offside in the build-up. Joao Cancelo equalised just before halftime and Yamal then set up Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon to score in the 50th and 53rd minutes. Karim Adeyemi completed the victory. ATLETICO STRIKE EARLY Atletico needed only 50 seconds to punish Manchester United's high defensive line, Alex Baena breaking clear down the left before squaring for Pablo Barrios to finish. United threatened through Bryan Mbeumo, who shot narrowly wide and later forced a close-range save from Jan Oblak, while Marcus Rashford also squandered an opportunity. Atletico had a Johnny Cardoso effort disallowed for a Marcos Llorente handball before the break and Julian Alvarez volleyed against the post early in the second half. United's task became harder when Yoro was sent off in the 74th minute for denying Jonathan David a goalscoring opportunity. Five minutes later, Ademola Lookman tapped into an empty net after David's shot was saved. Arsenal had to wait until the 64th minute for Jurrien Timber to break Lille's resistance from Noni Madueke's pass. Substitute Bukayo Saka then set up Eberechi Eze's goal before Kai Havertz supplied Saka for the third in the 71st minute. Villarreal recovered to beat Napoli 3-1 with goals from Georges Mikautadze, Santiago Mourino and Tanitoluwa Oluwaseyi. Brajan Gruda's 75th-minute strike gave RB Leipzig a 1-0 win over PSV Eindhoven after goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt saved Ivan Perisic's early penalty with his boot. Earlier, Sabah Baku beat Slavia Prague 2-0 through second-half goals from Kaheem Parris and Joy-Lance Mickels, while Luis Suarez and Issa Doumbia secured Sporting's 2-0 victory at Lens.

item.title: Edison drops as Muddy Waters alleges willful misconduct in Eaton Fire case
item.description: Edison International shares fell over 3% on Tuesday after short seller Muddy Waters said it had uncovered new information suggesting the utility acted with "conscious" or "willful" disregard in the Eaton Fire.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Edison International (EIX.N) shares fell over 3% on Tuesday after short seller Muddy Waters said it had uncovered new information suggesting the utility acted with "conscious" or "willful" disregard in the Eaton Fire. The investment firm said Edison could face at least $4 billion in fire-related damages, with potential liability reaching about $20 billion if a court determines the firm's conduct amounted to willful misconduct. Here are more details: Muddy Waters said the utility's Southern California Edison unit failed to fix deficiencies in a wildfire risk model despite allegedly knowing for about five years that it could not adequately account for high-wind conditions. The unit faces multiple [USN:L1N3UR0PG TEXT:"lawsuits"] alleging its electrical equipment [USN:L1N4410ZS TEXT:"started"] the Eaton Fire, which ignited on January 7, 2025, in the Los Angeles area. "We remain confident we will be able to show we acted as a reasonable utility would in maintaining the system in a safe manner," Edison spokesperson David Eisenhauer said. Edison has previously said it is cooperating with investigations into the cause of the fire and denied negligence or wrongdoing. Muddy Waters said the utility's failure to address the modeling issues increased wildfire risks during extreme wind events and was a factor in its assessment of the company's potential exposure.

item.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
item.description: Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have worsened sharply in recent months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage and accused Tokyo of using media correspondents to gather intelligence, marking a new low in bilateral relations that have worsened sharply in recent months. Russia's Foreign Ministry identified the journalist as Yuki Imai and the FSB security agency said he worked for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, which is a regional newspaper for Japan's northern island. He was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region the day before he planned to leave the country, the FSB said without specifying the date. It accused him of collecting and storing information on Russia's defence capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security. The Hokkaido Shimbun did not confirm the journalist's identity, saying only that it was still confirming details and that the reporter's safety was its top priority. JAPAN SUMMONS RUSSIAN AMBASSADOR Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said on Wednesday that Tokyo had asked Russian authorities for information and called for fair treatment and humanitarian consideration for the national. A senior official of the Japanese Foreign Ministry later summoned the Russian ambassador to Japan and lodged a protest for detaining the Japanese national and unilaterally issuing statements regarding the matter without providing explanation to Tokyo, the ministry said in a statement. The director-general of the Foreign Ministry's European Affairs Bureau, Kimitake Nakamura, also asked the ambassador, Nikolay Nozdrev, to set up an opportunity swiftly to meet the detained journalist, the ministry said. In a Russian state TV video report, three masked men in black uniforms handcuffed a man lying on the ground as a voice off camera said he was suspected of spying. The video showed the man being accompanied by two FSB servicemen onto a plane, then in a cage in a Moscow court, which ordered him detained for nearly two months. It is the most high-profile detainment of a foreign journalist since the 2023 detention of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich. Gershkovich, who says his arrest was a carefully planned [USN:L8N45H0MA TEXT:"FSB sting"], was found guilty of espionage by a Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024. LONG-RUNNING TENSIONS The case adds to long-running tensions between Russia and Japan, which have yet to sign a formal World War Two peace treaty due to a territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories. Those tensions heightened when Japan joined Western sanctions against Moscow over the war in Ukraine, with Russia regarding Japan as an [USN:L8N3ZG0NU TEXT:""unfriendly" country"]. But business ties remain with Japan a purchaser of Russian liquefied natural gas. Then in August, Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L8N44F0CG TEXT:"visited"] one of the disputed islands, causing an uproar in Japan. On Tuesday, a delegation from a Chinese province visited the same island, in what appeared to signal closer coordination between Moscow and Beijing in their criticism of Tokyo. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said on Tuesday that Japan had refused to consider Moscow's concerns about what she called Tokyo's "remilitarisation". She criticised Japan's alleged use of accredited journalists in Russia to gather information that could undermine Russian security. "We have to note that what has occurred will become an additional factor clouding the atmosphere of Russian-Japanese relations," Zakharova said. Asked whether improving relations between Russia and the US and Japan's purchases of LNG from Russia made it difficult for Tokyo to take countermeasures, Japan's Kihara said: "It is true that there are many issues between Japan and Russia. "From Japan's perspective, despite the difficult situation in Japan-Russia relations, Japan has taken resolute measures based on its position. At the same time, Russia is a neighbouring country to Japan, and communication is necessary to resolve these issues."

item.title: July 2025 easyJet threat video shared as September 2026
item.description: A video showing passengers restraining a man after he shouted “Death to America”, “Death to Trump” and “Allahu Akbar” aboard an easyJet flight in July 2025 has been miscaptioned online as an incident in September 2026.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A video showing passengers restraining a man after he shouted “Death to America”, “Death to Trump” and “Allahu Akbar” aboard an easyJet flight in July 2025 has been miscaptioned online as an incident in September 2026. Here are the key details: A September 29 X post described the footage as “Recorded earlier today aboard a Domestic internal flight EasyJet over The UK”, adding, “Legacy Media aren’t showing you this!!” A different X user posted the same footage on July 27, 2025, saying a friend recorded it and that the incident had occurred on an easyJet flight that morning. The same day, Police Scotland said in a statement that officers arrested and charged a 41-year-old man following reports of a disturbance on a Glasgow-bound flight on the morning of July 27, 2025. An easyJet spokesperson also said that day police removed a passenger from flight EZY609 from Luton to Glasgow on July 27 “due to their behaviour onboard”, STV reported . Abhay Nayak appeared at Paisley Sheriff Court on July 28, 2025, charged with assault and endangering the safety of an aircraft following the flight disturbance. He entered no plea and was remanded in custody, STV and other media outlets reported. An easyJet spokesperson told Reuters by email that no similar incident had occurred on an easyJet flight in September 2026. Reuters found no evidence of a matching incident reported on an easyJet flight in September 2026. A third-party court activity website lists an October 5, 2026 adjourned hearing at Glasgow High Court under the name “Abhay Devdas Nayak” as the most recent proceeding in the 2025 case. The Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service told Reuters the case “is scheduled to call for a Preliminary Hearing on 18 November 2026 at Glasgow HC.” Police Scotland did not respond to a request for comment. Verdict: Miscaptioned. The video shows an incident in July 2025, not September 2026. (This article was updated on October 14, 2026, to include easyJet’s comment in paragraph 8.) This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: London stocks flat ahead of key data releases; miners weigh
item.description: London's main stock indexes were little changed on Tuesday, with losses in industrials and mining offsetting gains in energy, as investors looked ahead to key economic data releases later in the week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 13 story has been corrected to clarify that the UK GDP data is due on Thursday, not Wednesday, in bullet point 11.) item.content:encoded: Le Nikkei finit en baisse de 0,05%  L'indice Nikkei a perdu 0,05% mercredi à 67.744,29 points. La pénurie de diesel pourrait se prolonger jusqu'en 2027 selon l'AIE LONDRES, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Les tensions sur l'approvisionnement en diesel pourraient persister jusqu'en 2027 en raison d'importantes réductions de stocks, contraires à la tendance saisonnière, qui se sont combinées à une production restreinte à l'approche du pic de demande hivernal, déclare l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) dans son rapport mensuel sur le marché pétrolier. FMI-Washington doit réduire son déficit et la Chine augmenter sa consommation intérieure BANGKOK, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Les États-Unis ne peuvent sortir de la spirale de l'endettement avec la seule croissance économique, Washington n'ayant pas d'autre choix que de procéder à des ajustements fiscaux ou budgétaires, a déclaré mercredi la directrice générale du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), Kristalina Georgieva. L'UE cherche à se rapprocher du Vietnam pour se fournir en minerais et se détourner de la Chine HANOÏ, 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'Union européenne cherche à s'approvisionner davantage en minéraux stratégiques auprès du Vietnam afin de réduire sa dépendance vis-à-vis de la Chine, selon des documents internes de l'UE consultés par Reuters. L'accord diesel entre Washington et Moscou est un "choix très risqué" selon Meloni ROME, 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'accord conclu entre Washington et Moscou concernant l'approvisionnement en diesel est un "choix très risqué", sapant les efforts visant à contraindre le président russe Vladimir Poutine à cesser sa guerre contre l'Ukraine, a déclaré mercredi la présidente du Conseil italien Giorgia Meloni. LVMH: Les ventes au T3 ravivent les doutes sur la reprise du secteur du luxe 13 octobre (Reuters) - Les ventes de la division Mode et Maroquinerie de LVMH, inférieures aux attentes au troisième trimestre en raison d'un affaiblissement de la demande des consommateurs chinois pour sa marque phare, Louis Vuitton, ravivent les interrogations sur les perspectives de reprise du secteur du luxe. Boeing a livré 57 avions en septembre, son meilleur mois depuis le début de l'année SEATTLE, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Boeing a annoncé mardi avoir livré 57 avions en septembre, après 51 en août et 55 un an plus tôt, marquant son meilleur résultat mensuel depuis le début de l'année. Citi: Bénéfice au-dessus des attentes au T3 avec la banque d'investissement, les services et la gestion de patrimoine 13 octobre (Reuters) - Citigroup a dépassé mardi les attentes de Wall Street concernant son bénéfice du troisième trimestre, porté par la hausse des revenus issus de la banque d'investissement, des transactions avec des multinationales, ainsi qu'à l'augmentation des résultats de la gestion de patrimoine. JP Morgan: Hausse du bénéfice au T3, mais l'élan de la banque d'investissement faiblit 13 octobre (Reuters) - JP Morgan a fait état mardi d'une hausse du bénéfice au troisième trimestre, tandis que le ralentissement récent des opérations de fusion-acquisition suscite des inquiétudes. Le bénéfice de Goldman Sachs progresse au T3 grâce à la bonne tenue des actions 13 octobre (Reuters) - Goldman Sachs a fait état mardi d'une hausse de son bénéfice au troisième trimestre, porté par une activité de fusions-acquisitions stable et par la volatilité des marchés liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient, qui a stimulé les revenus liés aux actions.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des frappes russes font 3 morts à Kyiv, infrastructures énergétiques ciblées KYIV, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Des frappes russes ont fait trois morts à Kyiv et ont endommagé nombre d'infrastructures énergétiques, plongeant des centaines de milliers de personnes dans le noir pendant la nuit de mardi à mercredi, ont déclaré les autorités. Explosions en Arabie saoudite, les Houthis répondent aux frappes de Ryad au Yémen RYAD, 13 octobre (Reuters) - De lourdes explosions ont retenti mardi soir près du siège de la compagnie pétrolière Saudi Aramco, pilier de l'économie saoudienne, ont rapporté six sources, dans un contexte d'escalade des hostilités entre l'Arabie saoudite et les Houthis, lesquels ont dit répondre à une attaque de Ryad contre la capitale yéménite Sanaa, qu'ils contrôlent. Sous pression, les dirigeants de l'UE envisagent d'agir face à la Chine BRUXELLES, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Les dirigeants de l'UE se réunissent jeudi à Bruxelles pour examiner l'avenir de leurs relations commerciales avec la Chine, dont les exportations en forte hausse de voitures et d'autres produits manufacturés menace l'industrie locale et risquent de provoquer des licenciements massifs à travers l'Europe. Grèce: L'ambassadrice des États-Unis remerciée après des informations de presse compromettantes WASHINGTON, 13 octobre (Reuters) - La Maison blanche a annoncé mardi avoir demandé à l'ambassadrice des États-Unis en Grèce de démissionner après des articles de presse indiquant elle aurait monnayé l'accès à des responsables de l'administration Trump en échange d'argent, de cadeaux et de faveurs. L'Iran utilise de nouvelles tactiques pour intensifier ses attaques avant les "midterms" aux USA selon des responsables iraniens DUBAÏ/LONDRES/WASHINGTON, 14 octobre (Reuters) - L'Iran met en oeuvre de nouvelles tactiques pour cibler les navires transitant par le détroit d'Ormuz, dans le but de maintenir les prix du pétrole à un niveau élevé et d'influencer les élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, ont déclaré deux hauts responsables iraniens à Reuters. Un ancien officier ukrainien va comparaître en Allemagne dans l'affaire Nord Stream HAMBOURG, 14 octobre (Reuters) - Un ancien officier de l'armée ukrainienne, accusé d'avoir participé aux explosions survenues en 2022 sur le gazoduc Nord Stream, doit comparaître mercredi devant un tribunal allemand. Le chef de la diplomatie américaine se rendra en Inde et en Ouzbékistan ce mois-ci WASHINGTON, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le secrétaire d'Etat américain Marco Rubio se rendra en Inde et en Ouzbékistan à la fin du mois, a annoncé mardi le département d'Etat. Un navire attaqué par un drone près de la Bulgarie, 11 marins disparus SOFIA, 13 octobre (Reuters) - Onze marins sont portés disparus mardi en mer Noire après le naufrage au large de la Bulgarie d'un navire touché par un drone. Le Hezbollah présente un plan d'aide aux Libanais déplacés 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le Hezbollah va verser une aide pouvant atteindre 14.000 dollars (12.500 euros) aux familles dont le domicile principal a été détruit ou rendu inhabitable au cours du conflit contre Israël cette année, a annoncé mardi le président du conseil exécutif du mouvement armé libanais. Le nombre de cas d'Ebola en RDC dépasse les 9.000, selon des données 13 octobre (Reuters) - Le nombre de cas confirmés d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) dépasse désormais les 9.000, selon des données gouvernementales publiées mardi.
